accountSetup.title: Connect to a Server & Create Your Account
accountSetup.narration: Setting up a SuiteLeaf account takes less than a minute, and your existing local files stay safe on your device. From your workspace home screen, click Connect to a server in the sidebar. Enter the address of your team's SuiteLeaf server—you don't even need to type https—and click Connect. SuiteLeaf opens the sign-in screen for that server. Click Create an account, enter your name, email address, and password, and submit. You land right in your team workspace with SuiteDrive ready for shared documents, spreadsheets, and presentations, while everything on your computer remains untouched whenever you disconnect.

storyboards.title: Write your first document
storyboards.summary: Sam just installed SuiteLeaf (or opened it in a browser) and wants to jot down a garden plan. Sam has used Word and Google Docs and expects the same basics: a blank page, a title, headings, bold, and no "did I save?" anxiety.

scenes.heading: Open SuiteLeaf
scenes.text: The home screen shows "New document", "New spreadsheet" and "New presentation" in one row, with the file library below. There's no sign-in.

scenes.heading: New document
scenes.text: A blank page opens with "Untitled document" as the title. The formatting toolbar fits on one row.

scenes.heading: Name it
scenes.text: Sam types "Garden plan" in the title box.

scenes.heading: Write
scenes.text: Sam clicks near the top of the page, types "Spring planting", presses Enter, and writes a sentence. The page stays put while Sam types.

scenes.heading: Heading
scenes.text: With the cursor on the first line, Sam picks Heading 1 from the paragraph style menu. The outline on the left lists it, aligned left like Google Docs.

scenes.heading: Bold
scenes.text: Sam double-clicks "last" and clicks Bold.

scenes.heading: Autosave
scenes.text: The status next to the title reads "Saved on this device". There's no Save button to remember.

scenes.heading: Reopen
scenes.text: Back to files shows "Garden plan" in the list, clear of the caption. Opening it shows the heading and the bold word intact.

storyboards.narration: Write your first document. Sam just installed SuiteLeaf (or opened it in a browser) and wants to jot down a garden plan. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open SuiteLeaf, New document, Name it, Write, and Heading.

storyboards.title: Find and organize your files
storyboards.summary: Maya runs the garden club's paperwork. She has a budget, a talk and a monthly newsletter. She wants to find any of them quickly, start next month's newsletter from this month's, and clear out what she no longer needs. She is used to Google Drive's search box and type filters.

scenes.heading: Empty library
scenes.text: The home screen says "A workspace waiting for you" and offers sample files. Maya opens Sample document, and it opens ready to edit.

scenes.heading: Add the club's files
scenes.text: Back on the home screen she uses New spreadsheet ("Garden club budget"), New presentation ("Garden club talk") and New document ("Garden club newsletter"). She types each name in the title box straight away, even while the spreadsheet grid is still loading, and every letter stays in the title. Each file saves automatically.

scenes.heading: Samples stay on offer
scenes.text: With four files listed (newest first, with today's edits showing the time), Explore a sample under the list still offers the sample document, budget and presentation.

scenes.heading: Search
scenes.text: Typing "garden" in Search your files replaces the welcome banner and New cards with Results for "garden": the three club files, right under the search box. Typing "harvest" finds the newsletter even though the word is only in its text, and quotes the matching line under its name. Escape clears the search and brings the home screen back.

scenes.heading: Filter by type
scenes.text: The sidebar's Documents shows the two documents and the heading changes to "Documents". Spreadsheets and Presentations each show one file. All files brings back all four.

scenes.heading: Sort
scenes.text: Clicking the Name column header sorts A to Z (an arrow shows the direction). Clicking Last edited goes back to newest first.

scenes.heading: Duplicate and rename
scenes.text: The copy icon on "Garden club newsletter" adds "Garden club newsletter copy". The pencil icon on the copy opens a Rename dialog, and Maya names it "Garden club newsletter - November" without opening it. Both newsletters are listed.

scenes.heading: Remove
scenes.text: The trash icon on "Welcome to SuiteLeaf" moves it to Trash, with Undo if that was a mistake. The sample leaves the list.

storyboards.narration: Find and organize your files. Maya runs the garden club's paperwork. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Empty library, Add the club's files, Samples stay on offer, Search, and Filter by type.

storyboards.title: Open a Word document
storyboards.summary: Lena was emailed "Office field notes.docx" by a colleague. She doesn't have Word and wants to read it, add a note and keep working on it, without uploading it anywhere. She also wants to know what might not have come across.

scenes.heading: Open / import
scenes.text: On the home screen Lena clicks Open / import and picks the .docx file.

scenes.heading: Editable copy
scenes.text: The document opens straight away, titled "Office field notes": a Heading 1 (also in the outline), a bold italic line in English, Chinese and Arabic, a "Reference" link, a table and "North plot: 40 m²" with a superscript ².

scenes.heading: Compatibility notes
scenes.text: A banner reads "Imported DOCX: Office field notes.docx , 2 compatibility notes". Opening it lists both: one link with an unsafe address (javascript:) was removed but its text was kept, and because SuiteLeaf lays out its own pages, Word's exact line and page breaks, floating placement and font styling may differ.

scenes.heading: Unsafe content dropped
scenes.text: "Unsafe link" is still there as plain text, but it is no longer a link. The normal https "Reference" link is kept.

scenes.heading: Edit
scenes.text: Lena clicks after "40 m²" and presses Enter. As in Word, the new line carries on the superscript, and the toolbar's Superscript button shows it is on. She clicks it to turn it off and types a review note in normal text.

scenes.heading: Autosave
scenes.text: The status reads "Saved on this device". The original .docx is never changed.

scenes.heading: Library
scenes.text: Back on the home screen, "Office field notes" is listed with her edit.

storyboards.narration: Open a Word document. Lena was emailed "Office field notes.docx" by a colleague. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open / import, Editable copy, Compatibility notes, Unsafe content dropped, and Edit.

storyboards.title: Write a long report and move around it with the outline
storyboards.summary: Tom is writing the community garden's annual report: a summary, the growing season, volunteers, the budget and next year's plans. It runs over two pages, and he wants to jump between sections without scrolling, as he does with Word's Navigation pane or the Google Docs outline.

scenes.heading: New document
scenes.text: Tom names it "Community garden annual report".

scenes.heading: Headings as he writes
scenes.text: He types each section title and picks Heading 1 or Heading 2 from the paragraph style menu, then writes the section. Each heading appears in the outline on the left as soon as it's styled.

scenes.heading: The shape of the report
scenes.text: Nine headings (five Heading 1, four Heading 2) are listed, with each Heading 2 indented under its Heading 1. The status bar reads "2 pages".

scenes.heading: Where am I?
scenes.text: Clicking Summary goes back to the top. As Tom scrolls down, the outline highlights the section he's reading.

scenes.heading: Jump
scenes.text: Clicking Expenses brings that heading to the top of the window, with a little space above it. It starts page 2 together with its paragraph rather than being left alone at the bottom of page 1.

scenes.heading: Edit in place
scenes.text: Clicking Volunteers jumps there. Tom adds a thank-you line under the heading, and it saves.

storyboards.narration: Write a long report and move around it with the outline. Tom is writing the community garden's annual report: a summary, the growing season, volunteers, the budget and next year's plans. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through New document, Headings as he writes, The shape of the report, Where am I?, and Jump.

storyboards.title: Add a table, a photo and a link
storyboards.summary: Asha is making a seed swap sign-up sheet: a short note, a table of who is bringing what, a photo from last year and a link to the club's rules. She expects to pick the table size, add rows as people sign up, and drop in a picture from her computer, as in Google Docs.

scenes.heading: Heading and note
scenes.text: In a new document, "Seed swap sign-up", Asha types a "Seed swap" Heading 1 and a line about the date and place.

scenes.heading: Insert table
scenes.text: Insert table opens a dialog. She sets 3 rows and 3 columns, leaves Header row ticked and clicks Create table.

scenes.heading: Fill it in
scenes.text: She types "Name / Bringing / Hoping for" and two sign-ups, pressing Tab to move between cells. The first row is a bold, shaded header.

scenes.heading: Add a row
scenes.text: Tab in the last cell adds a fourth row, and she adds Joy's sign-up.

scenes.heading: Insert a row in the middle
scenes.text: Priya signed up before Joy. Asha right-clicks Marek's row; a table menu offers insert row above/below, insert column left/right, delete row/column/table and the header row toggle. Insert row below adds a row under Marek, and she fills in Priya's sign-up.

scenes.heading: Keep writing below
scenes.text: She clicks below the table and types "Last year's swap table:".

scenes.heading: Insert image
scenes.text: Insert image opens the file picker. She chooses a PNG and it appears below the line, outside the table, with the caret after it so she can keep typing.

scenes.heading: Link
scenes.text: She types "Full rules are on the club website.", selects "club website" and clicks Insert link. SuiteLeaf's link dialog shows the text and she types example.org/seed-swap (no https:// needed) and clicks Apply. The words become a blue, underlined link to https://example.org/seed-swap.

scenes.heading: Resize the photo
scenes.text: She clicks the photo; corner handles appear. Dragging a corner shrinks it and it keeps its proportions.

scenes.heading: Saved
scenes.text: The status reads "Saved on this device". The sheet shows the table, photo and link together.

storyboards.narration: Add a table, a photo and a link. Asha is making a seed swap sign-up sheet: a short note, a table of who is bringing what, a photo from last year and a link to the club's rules. storyboards.title: Fix a repeated typo with find and replace
storyboards.summary: Priya wrote a thank-you letter to the garden volunteers and spelled "receive" as "recieve" three times. She wants to check the first one, then fix the rest in one go, the cautious way Google Docs and Word guides recommend.

scenes.heading: Write the letter
scenes.text: Priya types six short lines into a new document, "Thank-you letter", with "recieve" in three of them. The last one falls near the end of a long line.

scenes.heading: Open the tool
scenes.text: Edit to Find and replace opens a dialog with Find, Replace with, and options for matching case, regular expressions (with a Help link) and ignoring diacritics.

scenes.heading: Find
scenes.text: Typing "recieve" highlights all three. The counter reads "1 of 3", and the current match is darker and outlined.

scenes.heading: Replace one
scenes.text: With "receive" in Replace with, Replace fixes the first and moves on. The counter reads "1 of 2".

scenes.heading: Step through
scenes.text: Next shows "2 of 2". That match is at the end of a line, where the dialog was sitting, so the dialog steps aside below it, as Word's does. Previous goes back to "1 of 2".

scenes.heading: Move the dialog
scenes.text: She drags the dialog by its title, as in Google Docs.

scenes.heading: Replace all
scenes.text: Replace all fixes the other two. The counter reads "No results", and the dialog says "Replaced 2 instances of “recieve” with “receive”."

scenes.heading: Done
scenes.text: She closes the dialog. All three read "receive", and the letter is saved.

storyboards.narration: Fix a repeated typo with find and replace. Priya wrote a thank-you letter to the garden volunteers and spelled "receive" as "recieve" three times. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Write the letter, Open the tool, Find, Replace one, and Step through.

storyboards.title: Set up pages and export for Word and the web
storyboards.summary: Ben takes the garden club's minutes. Some members want a Word file they can print, with the club's name at the top of every page and page numbers. The club website wants a web page. Ben wants to write once and send both.

scenes.heading: Write the minutes
scenes.text: In "October meeting minutes", Ben adds a Heading 1, the attendance and the decisions.

scenes.heading: Page breaks
scenes.text: On an empty line he clicks Page break on the toolbar. The view moves to the new page with the cursor at its top, and he types "Appendix A: plot assignments". For Appendix B he uses Insert to Page break (shortcut Ctrl+Enter, or ⌘+Enter on a Mac). The status bar reads "3 pages".

scenes.heading: Page setup
scenes.text: File to Page setup… (also on the toolbar) opens a dialog with paper size, orientation, margins, header, footer and page numbers. He types the header "Riverside Garden Club" and the footer "Minutes: draft for members". Page numbers is off, as in Docs and Word, so he turns it on and clicks Apply.

scenes.heading: Check the pages
scenes.text: Where pages 1 and 2 meet, page 1 ends with the footer and "1 / 3", and page 2 starts with the header.

scenes.heading: Export DOCX
scenes.text: File to Export DOCX downloads "October meeting minutes.docx". Inside the file are the header and the footer with page-number fields.

scenes.heading: Export HTML
scenes.text: File to Export HTML downloads "October meeting minutes.html": the club name above the minutes, the footer below, and the headings and text in between.

storyboards.narration: Set up pages and export for Word and the web. Ben takes the garden club's minutes. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Write the minutes, Page breaks, Page setup, Check the pages, and Export DOCX.

storyboards.title: Carry a file to another computer
storyboards.summary: Sofia writes a packing list in SuiteLeaf on her laptop's browser and wants to keep working on it at the office. There's no account or cloud sync in single-node mode, so she needs one file she can email to herself or put on a USB stick, and to be sure that file holds everything.

scenes.heading: Write
scenes.text: Sofia makes "Lisbon trip packing list" with a Heading 1 and four bullet points. It autosaves in the browser.

scenes.heading: Download
scenes.text: Download in the header (its tooltip names the file) saves "Lisbon trip packing list.sldoc", a single SuiteLeaf file. The save status then reads Downloaded "Lisbon trip packing list.sldoc", so she knows what she got even if the browser saves it quietly.

scenes.heading: Remove it here
scenes.text: Back on the home screen, she moves the list to Trash, then deletes it forever. The dialog says: "Lisbon trip packing list" will be deleted from this browser forever. This can't be undone. A copy you downloaded isn't affected: open it again with Open / import. She confirms, and the library is empty, like a computer that has never seen it.

scenes.heading: Open on the other computer
scenes.text: Open / import with the .sldoc file opens it straight away, with the same title, the heading and all four items. The status says Opened "Lisbon trip packing list.sldoc" , Saved on this device.

scenes.heading: Keep going
scenes.text: She adds "Sunglasses" to the list, and it saves on this computer.

scenes.heading: Open it again by mistake
scenes.text: Later she opens the emailed file a second time. The list is already in this browser with newer changes, so instead of quietly making a copy SuiteLeaf asks: "Lisbon trip packing list" is already in this browser, shows when each was saved, warns that replacing discards the newer changes, and offers Cancel, Replace and Keep both (the safe choice is the main button). She cancels, and the list still ends with Sunglasses.

storyboards.narration: Carry a file to another computer. Sofia writes a packing list in SuiteLeaf on her laptop's browser and wants to keep working on it at the office. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Write, Download, Remove it here, Open on the other computer, and Keep going.

storyboards.title: Build a household budget with formulas
storyboards.summary: Maya wants to see her month at a glance: what she planned for each category, what she actually spent, and how much is left. She has never written a formula longer than a SUM and doesn't want a template full of tabs she doesn't understand.

scenes.heading: New spreadsheet
scenes.text: From the home screen Maya clicks "New spreadsheet". An empty grid opens as "Untitled spreadsheet".

scenes.heading: Name it
scenes.text: She types "October budget" in the title box.

scenes.heading: Enter the table
scenes.text: She clicks A1 and types Category, Planned and Spent, then five categories (Rent, Groceries, Utilities, Transport, Fun money) with their amounts. Tab moves across; Enter after the last amount returns to column A of the next row, as in Sheets and Excel, so she never reaches for the mouse.

scenes.heading: Totals with a suggestion
scenes.text: In row 7 she types "Total", Tab, then =su. Suggestions open with SUM first; Tab picks it and shows SUM(Number 1, [Number 2, …]) as a hint. She finishes B2:B6) and presses Tab. The cell shows 2280.

scenes.heading: Typing straight past a suggestion
scenes.text: In C7 she types =SUM(C2:C, and suggestions for "C" (COUNT, COUNTA, …) open. She keeps typing 6) and presses Enter at once. The cell keeps exactly =SUM(C2:C6) and shows 2077.

scenes.heading: What's left
scenes.text: In row 9 she types "Left to spend" and =B7-C7 (203). Clicking B9 shows the formula in the formula bar.

scenes.heading: Update a value
scenes.text: After a big grocery run she clicks C3 and changes Groceries' Spent from 380 to 455. The Spent total becomes 2152 (clicking C7 shows =SUM(C2:C6)) and Left to spend drops to 128 immediately.

scenes.heading: Autosave and keep a copy
scenes.text: The status reads "Saved on this device". Download saves a portable copy.

storyboards.narration: Build a household budget with formulas. Maya wants to see her month at a glance: what she planned for each category, what she actually spent, and how much is left. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through New spreadsheet, Name it, Enter the table, Totals with a suggestion, and Typing straight past a suggestion.

storyboards.title: Sort a column without moving the header
storyboards.summary: Lena coordinates volunteers and keeps their hours in a small table. She wants the busiest volunteers at the top, but in other apps sorting the Hours column dragged the "Hours" header into the middle of the list, or scrambled names away from their hours.

scenes.heading: Open the sheet
scenes.text: Lena opens "Volunteer hours" (Name, Team, Hours, eight volunteers).

scenes.heading: Select the whole table
scenes.text: She drags across A1:C9, header included, so each row stays together.

scenes.heading: Sort range
scenes.text: She chooses Data › Sort range.

scenes.heading: The header is recognised
scenes.text: "Sort range from A1 to C9" opens with "Data has header row" already ticked, because row 1 is text above a column of numbers. The "Sort by" list shows the header names (Name, Team, Hours) instead of column letters.

scenes.heading: Pick the column and order
scenes.text: She picks Hours and Z to A, then clicks Sort.

scenes.heading: Result
scenes.text: Row 1 still reads Name, Team, Hours. Wen Zhou (Greeters, 31) is first and Grace Obi (Setup, 7) is last; every name kept its own team and hours.

storyboards.narration: Sort a column without moving the header. Lena coordinates volunteers and keeps their hours in a small table. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the sheet, Select the whole table, Sort range, The header is recognised, and Pick the column and order.

storyboards.title: Filter to what matters
storyboards.summary: Jo runs a small online shop and keeps orders in a spreadsheet. Each morning she only cares about orders that are still Pending. She wants to hide the rest for a few minutes, not delete them or copy them somewhere else.

scenes.heading: Open the orders
scenes.text: Jo opens "Shop orders": Order, Customer, Status and Total for ten orders.

scenes.heading: Create a filter
scenes.text: She selects A1:D11 and clicks the funnel in the toolbar ("Create a filter"). Each header cell gets a filter button and the funnel shows as pressed.

scenes.heading: What everything adds up to
scenes.text: She drags down the Total column (D2:D11). The status bar reads Sum: 615.44 for all ten orders.

scenes.heading: Open the Status filter
scenes.text: Its panel offers Ascending/Descending, By Values, By Colors and By Conditions. By Values lists Cancelled (2), Pending (4) and Shipped (4).

scenes.heading: Pick values
scenes.text: Clicking the name "Shipped" unticks it (6/10), as it would in Sheets. Hovering Pending reveals "Filter Only", which keeps just Pending in one click (4/10). She confirms.

scenes.heading: Just the pending orders
scenes.text: Four rows remain (#1042, #1045, #1047, #1050). The row numbers skip (1, 3, 6, 8, 11), which shows the other rows are hidden, not deleted. The Status filter button turns solid.

scenes.heading: What's still to ship
scenes.text: With the Total column still selected, the status bar drops to Sum: 228.44, counting only the visible orders.

scenes.heading: Clear it
scenes.text: She reopens the Status filter and clicks "Clear Filter". All ten orders are back and the sum returns to 615.44.

scenes.heading: Remove the filter
scenes.text: Data › Remove filter (the funnel does the same) removes the filter buttons.

storyboards.narration: Filter to what matters. Jo runs a small online shop and keeps orders in a spreadsheet. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the orders, Create a filter, What everything adds up to, Open the Status filter, and Pick values.

storyboards.title: Freeze the header row
storyboards.summary: Chris is checking a 60-guest wedding list for the caterer. Halfway down, the column headings scroll away and it's no longer obvious which column is the meal choice and which is the RSVP.

scenes.heading: Open the list
scenes.text: "Wedding guest list" has Guest, Party size, Meal and RSVP for 60 guests.

scenes.heading: The problem
scenes.text: Chris scrolls down past row 35 and the header row is gone.

scenes.heading: View › Freeze
scenes.text: Back at the top, Chris opens View › Freeze, laid out as in Google Sheets: No rows, 1 row, 2 rows, Up to row n (the selected row), then the same four choices for columns. A tick shows the current freeze ("No rows"). Chris picks 1 row.

scenes.heading: Scroll with headers
scenes.text: A grey line appears under row 1. Scrolling down to the last guest in row 61, Guest, Party size, Meal and RSVP stay at the top.

scenes.heading: Reopen
scenes.text: Chris goes back to the file list and opens the workbook again. Row 1 is still frozen, and View › Freeze shows the tick next to 1 row. Choosing "No rows" would undo it.

storyboards.narration: Freeze the header row. Chris is checking a 60-guest wedding list for the caterer. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the list, The problem, View › Freeze, Scroll with headers, and Reopen.

storyboards.title: Format money and percentages
storyboards.summary: Jess is a freelance designer turning last month's hours into an invoice summary. The math is done, but 1020 and 0.54255… don't look like something to send a client. She wants dollar amounts, readable percentages, and a clear header and total.

scenes.heading: New spreadsheet
scenes.text: Jess names it "September invoice".

scenes.heading: Enter the work
scenes.text: Service, Hours, Rate, Amount and Share for three services, with Amount =B2*C2 and Share =D2/D$5, plus a Total row with SUMs. Rates show as 85, amounts as 1020, and shares as long decimals (0.5425531915), rounded to fit the column like Sheets' Automatic format.

scenes.heading: Currency
scenes.text: She selects C2:D5 and clicks $ ("Format as currency"). The cells read $85.00, $1,020.00 … $1,880.00.

scenes.heading: Percent
scenes.text: She selects E2:E5, clicks % ("Format as percent"), then "Increase decimal places". Shares read 54.3%, 29.8%, 16.0% and 100.0%.

scenes.heading: Bold
scenes.text: She drags across the header row and clicks the toolbar's B button, which then shows as pressed, then does the same for the Total row.

scenes.heading: Center the headings
scenes.text: With the header row selected she chooses Format › Align center.

scenes.heading: The value is unchanged
scenes.text: Selecting D2 shows =B2*C2 in the formula bar, and the B button is no longer pressed because D2 isn't bold. Formatting only changed how it looks.

storyboards.narration: Format money and percentages. Jess is a freelance designer turning last month's hours into an invoice summary. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through New spreadsheet, Enter the work, Currency, Percent, and Bold.

storyboards.title: Turn a table into a chart
storyboards.summary: Priya presents the quarterly studio budget on Friday. A table of numbers won't land with the room; she wants a column chart comparing Budget and Actual for each team, placed next to the table, that stays right when last-minute numbers change.

scenes.heading: Open the budget
scenes.text: Priya opens the "Sample budget" (Quarterly studio budget: Category, Budget, Actual, Remaining).

scenes.heading: Select with headers
scenes.text: She drags from A1 to C5: the four teams with their Budget and Actual columns, header row included.

scenes.heading: Insert chart
scenes.text: She clicks Insert chart on the toolbar. The panel opens below the toolbar, fills Source range with A1:C5 and suggests "Budget and Actual" as the title. She types "Studio costs by team" and keeps Column / bar.

scenes.heading: The chart
scenes.text: A column chart appears below the table with a Budget/Actual legend in source order, a value axis on round steps (0, 2000 … 12000) and a "Category" axis label.

scenes.heading: Move it
scenes.text: She drags the chart up beside the table, its top level with the header row.

scenes.heading: Resize it
scenes.text: She drags the bottom-right handle inward to make it smaller.

scenes.heading: Change the data
scenes.text: She clicks C3 and updates Engineering's Actual from 10800 to 13500. Remaining shows −1500, and the Engineering Actual bar grows past its Budget bar straight away; the axis rescales to 15000.

scenes.heading: Edit later
scenes.text: She double-clicks the chart. Edit chart opens with its title, Source range A1:C5 and type, ready for when the range needs to grow, and she closes it.

storyboards.narration: Turn a table into a chart. Priya presents the quarterly studio budget on Friday. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the budget, Select with headers, Insert chart, The chart, and Move it.

storyboards.title: Summarize spending with a pivot table
storyboards.summary: Ana and Ben log every shared household expense: date, category, who paid, amount. At the end of the month they want one small table showing how much went to each category and who paid, without writing SUMIFS formulas.

scenes.heading: Open the log
scenes.text: "Household expenses" has twelve rows: Date, Category, Paid by, Amount. Ana formats the Amount column as currency.

scenes.heading: Insert › Pivot table
scenes.text: Ana selects A1:D13 and chooses Insert › Pivot table. The panel's Source range reads A1:D13.

scenes.heading: Set it up
scenes.text: Title "October by category"; Rows: Category; Columns: Paid by. Value field is already Amount (the first numeric column) and Summarize by is SUM.

scenes.heading: Create
scenes.text: A new tab "October by category" opens, with a lock on its tab and a bar above the grid: "Pivot table from Sheet1 A1:D13 , Updates when the source changes", with Edit, Refresh and Make editable copy. It shows Category down the side, Ana and Ben across the top, and a bold Grand Total row and column, all in the source's dollar format. Groceries is $245.05 for Ana, $117.80 for Ben, $362.85 in total; the overall total is $760.74.

scenes.heading: Fix a typo in the source
scenes.text: Back on Sheet1, Ben corrects the Oct 1 grocery run from $84.20 to $148.20.

scenes.heading: The pivot follows
scenes.text: Back on the pivot tab there is nothing to refresh: Ana's Groceries is already $309.05 and the overall total $824.74.

scenes.heading: Editable copy
scenes.text: Make editable copy creates a plain worksheet, "October by category (copy)", with the same numbers, bold header and totals, and dollar format. Ana types a note beside Groceries.

storyboards.narration: Summarize spending with a pivot table. Ana and Ben log every shared household expense: date, category, who paid, amount. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the log, Insert › Pivot table, Set it up, Create, and Fix a typo in the source.

storyboards.title: Import and export a CSV without losing leading zeros
storyboards.summary: Rosa volunteers for a community garden. The old signup site exports members as a CSV, and member IDs like 00412 matter: the last time someone opened it in a spreadsheet the zeros vanished and the IDs stopped matching. She needs to update one member and send the CSV back.

scenes.heading: Open / import
scenes.text: From the home screen Rosa opens garden-members.csv (Member ID, Name, ZIP, Plot, Dues paid).

scenes.heading: Preview

scenes.heading: Zeros intact

scenes.heading: Update a member
scenes.text: Mei Chen paid at the work day; Rosa changes her Dues paid from 0 to 45.

storyboards.title: Review a budget with notes and comments
storyboards.summary: Alex is reviewing the studio budget before handing it to Jordan, who owns the Research line. Alex wants to leave two kinds of annotation: a quiet explanation of why Engineering's actual is so high, and a question that Jordan should answer.

scenes.heading: Open the budget
scenes.text: Alex opens the "Sample budget" (Quarterly studio budget).

scenes.heading: Add a note
scenes.text: With C3 (Engineering, Actual) selected, Alex chooses Sheet tools › "Add or edit cell note" and types "Includes the contractor invoice from September."

scenes.heading: Read it back
scenes.text: Alex jumps to G12 with the name box. The note closes, and C3 keeps a small corner marker. Hovering C3 pops up the note; moving away hides it.

scenes.heading: Sign comments
scenes.text: Alex chooses Sheet tools › "Your name on comments…", types "Alex" and clicks Save. The name is kept on this computer. Until a name is set, your own comments show "You". When you're signed in to a SuiteLeaf server, your account name is used and this item is hidden.

scenes.heading: Ask a question
scenes.text: With D3 (Engineering, Remaining) selected, Alex clicks the toolbar's "Insert comment" button. The draft is already signed "Alex". Alex types "Jordan, Engineering is $1,200 under budget. Can Research use $600 of it for the user study?" and clicks Comment.

scenes.heading: Comments panel
scenes.text: The speech-bubble button at the top right opens "Comment Management". It lists the thread under "D3 , Sheet1", signed "Alex", with the time.

scenes.heading: Share
scenes.text: Alex downloads the file for Jordan. The note and the signed thread are saved inside it.

scenes.heading: Jordan replies
scenes.text: On their own computer (off camera), Jordan opens the copy. The question still reads "Alex". Jordan replies "Yes, Research will take the $600. Thanks!" and sends the file back.

scenes.heading: Read the reply
scenes.text: Alex opens Jordan's copy. In the Comments panel, Jordan's reply sits under Alex's question, and each is signed by its writer. Clicking the thread highlights D3 in orange and opens a "Reply or add others with @" box. The tick resolves the thread and the bin deletes it.

storyboards.narration: Review a budget with notes and comments. Alex is reviewing the studio budget before handing it to Jordan, who owns the Research line. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the budget, Add a note, Read it back, Sign comments, and Ask a question.

storyboards.title: Highlight and check off tasks
storyboards.summary: Sofia is organizing the school bake sale with two other parents. She wants a to-do list where each task has a checkbox, and ticking it shades the whole row and crosses it out, so what's left stands out.

scenes.heading: Open the list
scenes.text: "Bake sale prep" has Done (empty), Task, Owner and Due for five tasks.

scenes.heading: Checkboxes
scenes.text: Sofia selects A2:A6 and chooses Insert › Checkbox. Each row gets an unticked checkbox, and, as in Google Sheets, each cell holds FALSE (the formula bar shows FALSE).

scenes.heading: Open conditional formatting
scenes.text: She selects A2:D6 and chooses Format › Conditional formatting. The side panel opens with "Manage: Entire Sheet" and an empty rule list. She clicks + to add a rule.

scenes.heading: Custom formula
scenes.text: Apply Range is already A2:D6. She sets Style Type to Custom Formula and types the usual Sheets recipe $A2=TRUE (the panel supplies the leading =).

scenes.heading: Style
scenes.text: The preview starts like Sheets' default: a light green fill that keeps the cells' own text colour. She turns on strikethrough, picks a softer green fill, and clicks Submit. The rule is listed as "Custom Formula, A2:D6".

scenes.heading: Tick tasks
scenes.text: She closes the panel and ticks "Book the school hall"; the formula bar now shows TRUE. She ticks "Order paper bags" too. Both rows turn green and are crossed out, with their text still black; the other three stay plain.

storyboards.narration: Highlight and check off tasks. Sofia is organizing the school bake sale with two other parents. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the list, Checkboxes, Open conditional formatting, Custom formula, and Style.

storyboards.title: Open an Excel workbook and send it back
storyboards.summary: Kemi runs a bakery. Her accountant emails the quarterly sales workbook as an .xlsx file. Kemi doesn't have Excel; she needs to open it, fix one number, and send back an Excel file that still has its formulas and formatting.

scenes.heading: Open / import
scenes.text: Kemi opens Q3 bakery sales.xlsx. It has two sheets, "Q3 sales" and "Summary".

scenes.heading: Import note
scenes.text: A bar above the toolbar reads "Imported XLSX: Q3 bakery sales.xlsx , 1 compatibility note". Expanding it explains that the workbook's 8 Excel formulas were kept with their last calculated results and that SuiteLeaf recalculates them with its own formula engine, so Excel-only functions may differ.

scenes.heading: Formatting came across
scenes.text: The peach header row, the bold Total row, dollar-formatted prices and revenue, the column widths and the frozen header are all there.

scenes.heading: Formulas came across
scenes.text: Selecting D3 shows =B3*C3.

scenes.heading: Fix a number
scenes.text: The accountant missed a late croissant order; Kemi changes Units sold in B3 from 958 to 1020. Croissant revenue becomes $3,315.00 and the total becomes $10,331.75.

scenes.heading: Cross-sheet formulas
scenes.text: The Summary tab (='Q3 sales'!D6 and an AVERAGE over the revenue column) already shows the new $10,331.75.

scenes.heading: Export XLSX
scenes.text: File › Export XLSX downloads "Q3 bakery sales.xlsx".

scenes.heading: Check before sending
scenes.text: Kemi opens the exported file again. The columns line up exactly as in the accountant's original, the header is still frozen, and the total is the corrected $10,331.75.

storyboards.title: Build a presentation
storyboards.summary: Priya volunteers at a community garden and has ten minutes to put together slides for Saturday's kickoff meeting. She has used Google Slides and PowerPoint and expects the same basics: a title slide, new slides from a layout menu, a splash of color, and dragging slides into order.

scenes.heading: New presentation
scenes.text: From the home screen Priya clicks "New presentation". The file title box reads "Untitled presentation", and the title slide shows grey "Click to add title" and "Click to add subtitle" placeholders.

scenes.heading: Name it
scenes.text: She types "Spring Garden Kickoff" in the file title box.

scenes.heading: Title slide
scenes.text: She clicks each placeholder and types "Spring Garden Kickoff" and "Community Garden , Saturday 10 am". The placeholder text disappears as she types; nothing has to be selected and deleted first.

scenes.heading: Title & body
scenes.text: "+ New slide" to "Title & body" adds slide 2 with empty title and text placeholders. She types "This season's plan" and three bullets.

scenes.heading: Change the layout
scenes.text: She adds another Title & body slide and types "How you can help". Two lists would read better side by side, so with nothing selected she picks Layout to Two columns. Her title stays at the top and an empty second column appears. She types Saturday jobs on the left and May events on the right.

scenes.heading: Section header
scenes.text: "+ New slide" to "Section header" adds a dark "Questions?" slide.

scenes.heading: Shape
scenes.text: On the title slide she clicks Circle, which draws a round circle, sets Fill to Yellow, and drags it into the top-right corner as a sun.

scenes.heading: Background
scenes.text: With nothing selected she picks Background to Sage green. The slide and its thumbnail turn soft green.

scenes.heading: Reorder
scenes.text: She drags the "How you can help" thumbnail up. A blue line shows where it will land, and on release it sits before "This season's plan".

scenes.heading: Autosave
scenes.text: The status reads "Saved on this device".

storyboards.narration: Build a presentation. Priya volunteers at a community garden and has ten minutes to put together slides for Saturday's kickoff meeting. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through New presentation, Name it, Title slide, Title & body, and Change the layout.

storyboards.title: Present with speaker notes
storyboards.summary: It's Saturday morning. Priya opens the garden kickoff slides she saved last night, jots a reminder under each slide, and presents them from her laptop. She's nervous about forgetting things, so the notes matter.

scenes.heading: Open the deck
scenes.text: On the home screen Priya clicks "Open / import" and picks "Spring Garden Kickoff.slslides". It opens with four slides.

scenes.heading: Speaker notes
scenes.text: Under the slide she clicks "Click to add speaker notes" and types "Welcome everyone. Thank the library for the room."

scenes.heading: A note per slide
scenes.text: She selects slides 2 and 3 in the thumbnails and adds a reminder to each.

scenes.heading: Start from the beginning
scenes.text: Still on slide 3, she opens the arrow next to Slideshow. The menu offers "Present from beginning" (Cmd+Shift+Enter), "Present from current slide" (Cmd+Enter), and "Present with speaker notes". She picks Present from beginning. The show opens in full screen on slide 1, and the controls fade after a moment.

scenes.heading: Rehearse with notes
scenes.text: She presses S. Her note for the slide appears beside it, with a timer and a preview of the next slide ("Next: This season's plan").

scenes.heading: Advance
scenes.text: The right arrow key moves to "This season's plan", then "How you can help". The notes change with the slide.

scenes.heading: Present
scenes.text: When people arrive, she presses S again so the slide fills the screen. Moving the mouse brings back Previous, "Slide 3 of 4", Next, Notes, and Exit. She clicks Next to reach "Questions?".

scenes.heading: End
scenes.text: Escape ends the show and leaves full screen. Back in the editor, the first slide's note is still there.

storyboards.narration: Present with speaker notes. It's Saturday morning. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the deck, Speaker notes, A note per slide, Start from the beginning, and Rehearse with notes.

storyboards.title: Connect to your team's server
storyboards.summary: Leo has been using SuiteLeaf on his own, with files on his computer. The garden club now runs a SuiteLeaf server so everyone can share files. The coordinator sent him the address, and Leo wants to join without losing what's already on his computer.

scenes.heading: Home on this computer
scenes.text: Leo's own files ("Tomato planting notes", "Allotment wish list") are listed under Your files. The sidebar says "Your workspace, in this browser." Settings, at the bottom of the sidebar, has "Connect to a server".

scenes.heading: Connect
scenes.text: Leo clicks it. The "Connect to a SuiteLeaf server" dialog explains that files on this computer stay here.

scenes.heading: Server address
scenes.text: He types the address he was given, without http://, and clicks Connect. SuiteLeaf tries https:// first, then http://.

scenes.heading: Sign in
scenes.text: The app reloads to a sign-in card showing the server's host name. It's his first time, so he clicks "Create an account".

scenes.heading: Create an account
scenes.text: He enters his name, email, and a password, then clicks "Create account".

scenes.heading: Team home
scenes.text: He lands on the team home screen ("YOUR TEAM WORKSPACE"). "Connect to a server" is gone.

scenes.heading: Who and where
scenes.text: The sidebar shows his full name and the server, with labeled Sign out and Disconnect buttons. A note says files are saved to SuiteDrive on the server and that his files on this computer are kept for when he disconnects.

scenes.heading: SuiteDrive
scenes.text: Below the New cards, SuiteDrive shows "This folder is empty." His local files are not mixed in.

storyboards.narration: Connect to your team's server. Leo has been using SuiteLeaf on his own, with files on his computer. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Home on this computer, Connect, Server address, Sign in, and Create an account.

storyboards.title: Start a document in SuiteDrive
storyboards.summary: Rosa coordinates the garden club's watering rota. She opens the team's SuiteLeaf server in her browser, wants a folder for club paperwork, and wants to write the rota there so everyone can find it. She works the way she does in Google Drive: make a folder, open it, click New.

scenes.heading: Open the server
scenes.text: Rosa goes to the server's address. Because the server serves the app, it opens straight to sign-in, with no "work on this computer" option. She creates her account.

scenes.heading: New folder
scenes.text: In SuiteDrive she clicks "New folder". A small SuiteLeaf dialog asks for the name, with "Untitled folder" selected. She types "Garden club" and clicks Create. It appears in My Drive.

scenes.heading: Open the folder
scenes.text: She clicks it. The path reads "My Drive › Garden club" and the folder is empty. The New document, New spreadsheet, and New presentation buttons now read "In Garden club".

scenes.heading: New document
scenes.text: She clicks "New document". A blank document opens, and she types the rota.

scenes.heading: Saved to SuiteDrive
scenes.text: The status next to the title changes to "Saved to SuiteDrive". There's no Save button.

scenes.heading: Rename
scenes.text: She types "Watering rota" in the title box. The status returns to "Saved to SuiteDrive".

scenes.heading: Find it again
scenes.text: "Back to files" returns her to the Garden club folder, where "Watering rota.sldoc" is waiting.

storyboards.narration: Start a document in SuiteDrive. Rosa coordinates the garden club's watering rota. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the server, New folder, Open the folder, New document, and Saved to SuiteDrive.

storyboards.title: Pick up on another server
storyboards.summary: The garden club runs two SuiteLeaf servers in one cluster: one at the office and one at the library. Priya starts a budget slide at the office, then that evening reaches the library server instead. She expects her account and her presentation to be there, just as OneDrive files show up on every computer.

scenes.heading: At the office
scenes.text: While the servers start, a caption sets the scene. Priya opens the office server and creates her account. The sign-in card says the server shares accounts and files with the organization's other servers.

scenes.heading: Which server
scenes.text: On the home screen, the sidebar names the server ("Files are saved to SuiteDrive on …") and reads "Connected to 1 other server".

scenes.heading: Make a slide
scenes.text: She creates a new presentation, names it "Budget update", and fills in the title slide. The top bar shows the office server's address next to a cloud icon, and the status reads "Saved to SuiteDrive".

scenes.heading: Switch servers
scenes.text: That evening she opens the library server's address. It's a different address, so she sees its sign-in card with its own host name and the note that an account made on any of the organization's servers works here.

scenes.heading: Sign in
scenes.text: She signs in with the email and password she created at the office.

scenes.heading: Her file is there
scenes.text: SuiteDrive lists "Budget update.slslides", with the time she saved it at the office.

scenes.heading: Keep working
scenes.text: She opens it. The top bar now shows the library server's address. She sees the subtitle she wrote at the office and adds ", Hoses $40". It saves to SuiteDrive on the library server.

storyboards.narration: Pick up on another server. The garden club runs two SuiteLeaf servers in one cluster: one at the office and one at the library. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through At the office, Which server, Make a slide, Switch servers, and Sign in.

storyboards.title: When someone else saved first
storyboards.summary: Sam is writing the bake sale flyer in SuiteDrive. Jordan, on another computer, opens the same flyer, changes the time, and saves. Sam doesn't know and keeps typing. Neither of them should lose work silently. Sam wants to choose between keeping both versions and taking Jordan's.

scenes.heading: Writing
scenes.text: Sam signs in to the garden club's server, creates "Bake sale flyer" and types "Bake sale on Saturday, 10 am to noon." The status reads "Saved to SuiteDrive".

scenes.heading: Jordan saves first
scenes.text: A caption explains that Jordan changes the time to "9 am to 1 pm" and saves from another computer. The recording simulates this by saving a new version through the SuiteDrive API, as another client would.

scenes.heading: Sam keeps typing
scenes.text: Sam adds "All proceeds go to new raised beds."

scenes.heading: The banner
scenes.text: A banner appears: "This file was changed in SuiteDrive after you opened it. A newer version was saved at 2:21 PM. Your edits weren't uploaded and are safe on this device. Save them as a copy to keep both versions, or reload the SuiteDrive version and discard your edits." The two choices sit together on the right, the safe one first: "Save as copy", then "Reload from SuiteDrive". The status reads "SuiteDrive has a newer version". Nothing was overwritten.

scenes.heading: Keep both
scenes.text: Sam clicks "Save as copy". The status reads "Saved a copy to SuiteDrive" and the banner goes away.

scenes.heading: Name the copy
scenes.text: The copy has the same name as the original, so Sam renames it "Bake sale flyer (Sam's draft)".

scenes.heading: Both in SuiteDrive
scenes.text: Back in SuiteDrive there are two files: "Bake sale flyer.sldoc" (Jordan's) and "Bake sale flyer (Sam's draft).sldoc".

scenes.heading: Again, take theirs
scenes.text: Sam opens Jordan's version, which shows the new time, "9 am to 1 pm", and starts adding "Bring a cake!" while Jordan saves another change. The banner returns.

scenes.heading: Reload
scenes.text: Sam clicks "Reload from SuiteDrive". SuiteLeaf asks "Discard your edits and open the newer version from SuiteDrive? Your edits will be lost." and Sam confirms. The document shows Jordan's "Saturday 14 June, 9 am to 1 pm", without Sam's unsaved line, and the status reads "Saved to SuiteDrive".

storyboards.narration: When someone else saved first. Sam is writing the bake sale flyer in SuiteDrive. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Writing, Jordan saves first, Sam keeps typing, The banner, and Keep both.

storyboards.title: Sign out and go back to this computer
storyboards.summary: Leo keeps a personal to-do list in SuiteLeaf on his computer and also uses the garden club's server for shared files. At the end of the day he wants to sign out of the server and go back to working on his computer alone. He wants his personal list untouched and the club's files left on the server.

scenes.heading: Personal file
scenes.text: Leo writes "Personal to-do" in single-node mode. It reads "Saved on this device".

scenes.heading: Connect
scenes.text: He connects to the team server and creates an account.

scenes.heading: Shared file
scenes.text: He creates "Shed inventory" in SuiteDrive. It reads "Saved to SuiteDrive".

scenes.heading: Separate lists
scenes.text: SuiteDrive lists "Shed inventory.sldoc". His personal list isn't mixed in.

scenes.heading: Account card
scenes.text: Under his name and the server's address are two labeled buttons: Sign out and Disconnect. Disconnect signs out and leaves the server in one step.

scenes.heading: Sign out
scenes.text: He clicks Sign out. The sign-in card says "You signed out of ‹server›. Your SuiteDrive files stay on the server." The server's files are behind it.

scenes.heading: Back to this computer
scenes.text: He clicks "Work on this computer without a server". The app returns to "Your workspace, in this browser." A notice says "Disconnected from ‹server› and signed out. Files in SuiteDrive stay on the server; connect again to open them."

scenes.heading: His files
scenes.text: "Your files" lists "Personal to-do". "Shed inventory" isn't there, because it lives on the server. The browser no longer holds his sign-in.

storyboards.narration: Sign out and go back to this computer. Leo keeps a personal to-do list in SuiteLeaf on his computer and also uses the garden club's server for shared files. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Personal file, Connect, Shared file, Separate lists, and Account card.

storyboards.title: Get back what you deleted
storyboards.summary: Maya is finishing the garden club newsletter on her laptop. She deletes the plant-sale paragraph by mistake and only notices after she has kept typing. In Google Docs she would open File, then Version history, then See version history, and click through timestamps that never say what changed. The history would also stay in Google's cloud, so a downloaded copy would not have it. She wants the missing paragraph back, and she wants that history to leave with the file.

scenes.heading: Write the newsletter
scenes.text: Maya creates "Garden club newsletter" and types "The plant sale is Saturday in the library hall." She pauses. She adds a second paragraph, "Bring seedlings and a bag for the basil." She pauses again. Each pause keeps a version.

scenes.heading: Open history in one click
scenes.text: A History button sits in the header, next to the title. She clicks it. A panel lists the versions, newest first. Each row has a time and a sentence about what changed ("Added a paragraph"), not only a clock time. The newest row is the document she is editing.

scenes.heading: Delete the second paragraph
scenes.text: She deletes "Bring seedlings and a bag for the basil." and pauses. The panel gains a row whose sentence is "Removed a paragraph."

scenes.heading: Preview the earlier version
scenes.text: She clicks the row from when both paragraphs were there. The document shows both sentences again. A banner says she is viewing an earlier version and offers Restore this version and Back to latest. The live newsletter is not overwritten yet.

scenes.heading: Name it
scenes.text: On that row she types the name "Before the library meeting" and saves the name. The row shows the name as well as the sentence about the change.

scenes.heading: Restore, and keep the shorter copy
scenes.text: She clicks Restore this version. Both paragraphs are back in the editor and she can type. The shorter newsletter stays in the list, so the restore itself can be undone from the same panel.

scenes.heading: Take the history with the file
scenes.text: She downloads the SuiteLeaf file. The named version and the deleted-paragraph version are inside that file, so opening it on another computer still shows the timeline.

storyboards.narration: Get back what you deleted. Maya is finishing the garden club newsletter on her laptop. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Write the newsletter, Open history in one click, Delete the second paragraph, Preview the earlier version, and Name it.

storyboards.title: Share a document with a teammate
storyboards.summary: Rosa wrote the garden club's "Watering rota" in SuiteDrive (storyboard 23). Sam swaps shifts every week, so he needs to edit it. Priya only needs to read it and leave the odd question. Rosa wants to give each of them the right access from inside the document, without learning a permissions system, and to take access away again when Priya leaves the club.

scenes.heading: Open the rota
scenes.text: Rosa is signed in to the club's server and opens "Watering rota". A blue Share button sits in the header next to the server name.

scenes.heading: Open Share
scenes.text: She clicks Share. A dialog titled Share “Watering rota” shows an "Add people" box and the list of people with access: "Rosa Diaz (you)" with her email, and Owner. A line under the list says "Only the people listed here can open this file." It also says the file is in Garden club.

scenes.heading: Find Sam
scenes.text: She types "sa". A suggestion shows "Sam Okafor" and sam@gardenclub.org. She picks him.

scenes.heading: Choose a role
scenes.text: A role control next to his name already reads Editor, "Can change anything", before she does anything else. She clicks Share. The dialog says "Sam can now edit" and lists him as Editor.

scenes.heading: Add Priya as a commenter
scenes.text: She types "priya", picks "Priya Shah", opens the role menu (Viewer "Can read", Commenter "Can read and comment", Editor "Can change anything"), chooses Commenter, and clicks Share. "Priya can now comment."

scenes.heading: Someone without an account
scenes.text: She types "lee@example.com". The dialog says "No account on this server uses lee@example.com. Ask them to sign up first." and the Share button stays disabled.

scenes.heading: Change and remove access
