scenes.heading: Folder access
scenes.text: She clicks Share “Garden club”, adds Sam as Editor, then reopens Share on the rota. The list is Rosa and "Sam Okafor , Editor , from Garden club". Priya is gone.

scenes.heading: Sam's side
scenes.text: Sam signs in. SuiteDrive's "Shared with me" lists "Watering rota.sldoc" with "Rosa Diaz , Can edit", without a reload. He opens it, adds "Thursday: ask Alex to cover.", and it saves to SuiteDrive.

scenes.heading: A viewer's side
scenes.text: Alex Rivera, who can only view, signs in. Shared with me says "Rosa Diaz , Can view". The rota opens with a "View only" label beside the title. The editing toolbar is greyed out, typing does nothing, and nothing tries to save.

storyboards.narration: Share a document with a teammate. Rosa wrote the garden club's "Watering rota" in SuiteDrive (storyboard 23). Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the rota, Open Share, Find Sam, Choose a role, and Add Priya as a commenter.

storyboards.title: Present from your laptop
storyboards.summary: Priya is about to give the garden club kickoff from her laptop, in a library room, with no second monitor. She wrote a reminder under each slide last night. In Google Slides the Slideshow button hides those notes, and Presenter view is a second window that often opens on the wrong screen. She needs the notes, the next slide, and a clock on this screen, and a way to fill the screen with only the slide when she turns the laptop toward the room.

scenes.heading: Open the deck
scenes.text: Priya opens a short presentation that already has speaker notes on the first slides.

scenes.heading: Present on this screen
scenes.text: She clicks Slideshow. Because the deck has notes, the show opens as presenter view in the same window: the current slide, the next slide, her notes in type large enough to read at arm's length, and a timer that is already running. She does not pick a second mode and no extra window appears.

scenes.heading: Read the note
scenes.text: The first note, "Welcome everyone. Thank the library for the room.", is on screen next to the slide, not hidden until she remembers a menu.

scenes.heading: Advance
scenes.text: The right arrow moves to the next slide. The note changes to that slide's note, the next-slide thumbnail updates, and the timer keeps counting.

scenes.heading: Turn the laptop toward the room
scenes.text: She presses N. The notes, the next slide, and the timer hide, and the current slide fills the window. She presses N again and the presenter view returns, on the same slide, with the timer still running.

scenes.heading: Black the screen
scenes.text: She presses B. The audience sees a black slide. Her notes stay visible. She presses B again and the slide comes back.

scenes.heading: Leave the show
scenes.text: Escape returns to the editor. The notes are still under the slides.

storyboards.narration: Present from your laptop. Priya is about to give the garden club kickoff from her laptop, in a library room, with no second monitor. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the deck, Present on this screen, Read the note, Advance, and Turn the laptop toward the room.

storyboards.title: Restore an earlier version
storyboards.summary: On Tuesday morning Sam rewrote the "Watering rota" for a new schedule the committee hadn't agreed. Rosa wants Monday evening's version back, but she also wants to see what Sam changed first, and she doesn't want to lose his work in case the committee changes its mind.

scenes.heading: Open the rota
scenes.text: Rosa signs in and opens "Watering rota" in Garden club. The page is Sam's rewrite. The header shows a clock labelled "Version history".

scenes.heading: Open the history
scenes.text: File › Version history shows the shortcut Cmd+Alt+Shift+H. She clicks the clock. A panel opens on the right: "Current version", "Today 09:14 , Sam Okafor", and "Yesterday 18:02 , Rosa Diaz". Sam's 09:10 and 09:06 autosaves are folded under an arrow on the 09:14 entry.

scenes.heading: Preview with changes
scenes.text: She clicks yesterday. The page is read-only. Compared with the current version, Sam's additions are underlined in green and his deletions struck through in red. The note says 4 paragraphs change. "Changes in this version" shows Monday's text on its own, because nothing is earlier.

scenes.heading: Name it
scenes.text: From the version's ⋯ menu she chooses "Name this version" and types "Agreed rota". "Named versions only" leaves just that entry. After a reload the name is still there.

scenes.heading: Restore
scenes.text: From the editor that is three clicks: the clock, "Agreed rota", and Restore this version. The note already says Restore "Agreed rota"? 4 paragraphs change. The current version stays in history.

scenes.heading: Back to editing
scenes.text: The panel closes, the page is Monday's rota, and the status reads "Saved to SuiteDrive". Opening the history again, the top entry is Restored "Agreed rota" , Rosa Diaz. Yesterday's named version and Sam's 09:14 entry are still in the list.

scenes.heading: Keep Sam's draft
scenes.text: She opens Sam's 09:14 version and chooses "Make a copy". In Garden club, next to the rota, is "Watering rota (Sam's draft, 12 Oct 09:14).sldoc". The date is the version's local date, so a recording on another day uses that day.

scenes.heading: Change her mind
scenes.text: Restoring the 09:14 version puts Sam's text back. The saved file is the same bytes as his 09:14 upload.

scenes.heading: Another server
scenes.text: Rosa signs in on the club's other server, opens the rota, and "Agreed rota" is still the name.

storyboards.narration: Restore an earlier version. On Tuesday morning Sam rewrote the "Watering rota" for a new schedule the committee hadn't agreed. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the rota, Open the history, Preview with changes, Name it, and Restore.

storyboards.title: Comment on a document
storyboards.summary: Jordan is reviewing Alex's "Quarterly Report" before it goes to the board. Jordan wants to point at specific sentences ("Is 12% right? Finance says 11.5%"), have Alex answer in the same thread, and close each point when it's settled. Alex works in Word, so the comments have to survive a trip through a .docx file and back.

scenes.heading: Open the report
scenes.text: Jordan opens "Quarterly Report" on their own computer.

scenes.heading: Comment on a phrase
scenes.text: Jordan selects "grew 12%" and presses Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+M. A comment card opens in the right margin, the comment box focused, and the phrase turns yellow.

scenes.heading: Name, then post
scenes.text: Jordan types "Is 12% right? Finance says 11.5%." and presses Cmd/Ctrl+Enter. The first comment on this computer asks for a name. Jordan types "Jordan" and presses Cmd/Ctrl+Enter again. The card shows Jordan, the time, and the question. Later comments skip the name.

scenes.heading: The highlight stays put
scenes.text: Typing before the phrase leaves the highlight on "grew 12%". Typing inside it extends the highlight. Splitting the paragraph keeps both pieces highlighted. Undo puts the sentence back.

scenes.heading: Second comment by button
scenes.text: Jordan selects "Outlook for the rest of the year" and clicks Add comment in the margin. No name is asked. Jordan writes "Can we shorten this?" and posts with Cmd/Ctrl+Enter.

scenes.heading: Close and reopen
scenes.text: Jordan goes back to the files and opens the report again. Both highlights and cards are still there.

scenes.heading: Send to Alex
scenes.text: Jordan chooses File › Export DOCX. The file carries both threads, on the same words, signed Jordan.

scenes.heading: Alex replies in Word
scenes.text: Alex replies "Yes, 11.5% , fixed", corrects the figure, and sends the file back. The recording shows that hand-off with a caption; SuiteLeaf then opens the file Alex sent.

scenes.heading: Import the reply
scenes.text: The banner reads "2 comment threads imported". The first card shows Alex's reply under Jordan's question, on "grew 11.5%".

scenes.heading: Resolve
scenes.text: Jordan clicks the tick. The highlight disappears and the card collapses to "Resolved by Jordan". Exporting again keeps that thread in the Word file, marked done.

scenes.heading: Find it again
scenes.text: The Comments button opens a panel with Open and Resolved tabs. Under Resolved, Jordan clicks the thread and Reopen brings the highlight and the reply back.

storyboards.narration: Comment on a document. Jordan is reviewing Alex's "Quarterly Report" before it goes to the board. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the report, Comment on a phrase, Name, then post, The highlight stays put, and Second comment by button.

storyboards.title: Get a deleted file back
storyboards.summary: Maya is cleaning up the garden club's files. She throws away the October newsletter, then realizes November still quotes it. In Google Drive, Trash sits in a side list, an Undo banner disappears after a few seconds, and anything left in Trash is deleted after 30 days whether she meant that or not. She wants the newsletter back, and she wants it to stay deleted only when she says so.

scenes.heading: The newsletter is in the library
scenes.text: Maya creates "Garden club newsletter" and returns to the home screen. It is listed under Your files.

scenes.heading: Move it to Trash
scenes.text: She clicks the trash icon on that row. There is no browser dialog. The newsletter leaves Your files. A banner stays on the page: the newsletter is in Trash, with Undo. The banner does not vanish on its own.

scenes.heading: Undo
scenes.text: She clicks Undo. The newsletter is back under Your files, and the banner is gone.

scenes.heading: Trash in the sidebar
scenes.text: She moves it to Trash again. Trash in the sidebar lists "Garden club newsletter". Your files does not.

scenes.heading: Restore
scenes.text: She clicks Restore. Trash is empty. All files shows the newsletter again.

scenes.heading: Delete forever, on purpose
scenes.text: She moves it to Trash once more, opens Trash, and clicks Delete forever. A dialog in the page names the file and offers Cancel and Delete forever. She confirms. The newsletter is gone from Trash and from the library.

storyboards.narration: Get a deleted file back. Maya is cleaning up the garden club's files. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The newsletter is in the library, Move it to Trash, Undo, Trash in the sidebar, and Restore.

storyboards.title: Suggest changes and accept them
storyboards.summary: Jordan is editing Alex's "Quarterly Report", but it's Alex's report, so Jordan wants every change to be a proposal that Alex can accept or turn down. Alex's manager reviews in Word with Track Changes, so the suggestions have to arrive in Word as tracked changes and come back the same way.

scenes.heading: Open the report
scenes.text: Jordan opens "Quarterly Report". A mode switch at the right of the toolbar reads "Editing", next to a name field.

scenes.heading: Switch to Suggesting
scenes.text: Jordan types the name Jordan and clicks Suggesting (Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+X does the same). The label turns green, reads "Suggesting", and stays in the toolbar and the status bar while Jordan scrolls.

scenes.heading: Suggest a few changes
scenes.text: Jordan types "approximately " before "40 customers" (green and underlined), deletes "very" (struck through in red), and makes "on budget" bold (a dotted underline).

scenes.heading: Suggestion cards
scenes.text: Each change has a card in the margin, with the author and time: "Jordan , Add “approximately”", "Delete “very”", "Format: bold". Each card has ✓ and ✗. Accept all and Reject all sit above the cards, so either is one click, and hovering previews the page.

scenes.heading: Still there after a reopen
scenes.text: Jordan goes back to the files and opens the report again. The three cards are still Jordan's, and the file is still in Suggesting.

scenes.heading: Plain text asks
scenes.text: File › Export TXT opens "Pending suggestions" and asks for the original text or the text with suggestions accepted. Nothing is chosen silently.

scenes.heading: Export to Word
scenes.text: File › Export DOCX. The file contains Jordan's insertion, deletion, and bold as Word tracked changes.

scenes.heading: Manager adds one
scenes.text: In Word the manager accepts the deletion and adds a tracked insertion, "(unaudited)". The file comes back.

scenes.heading: Import
scenes.text: Jordan opens the returned .docx. The import summary says "3 suggestions imported", and the file opens in Suggesting. Cards show Jordan's remaining insertion and formatting change, and the manager's insertion signed "Alex's manager".

scenes.heading: Review
scenes.text: Alex opens Tools › Review suggestions. The panel reads "3 suggestions". Alex accepts "approximately" and rejects the bold, one click each.

scenes.heading: Preview and accept the rest
scenes.text: Alex hovers Accept all, the page shows "Preview: suggestions accepted" with the markup hidden, and Alex clicks it. Cmd/Ctrl+Z brings the accepted suggestion back, and Alex accepts it again.

scenes.heading: Back to editing
scenes.text: Alex switches to Editing. Reopening the file later opens in Editing, because that was the last mode used. The report reads "We now serve approximately 40 customers and the project is on budget. (unaudited)".

storyboards.narration: Suggest changes and accept them. Jordan is editing Alex's "Quarterly Report", but it's Alex's report, so Jordan wants every change to be a proposal that Alex can accept or turn down. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the report, Switch to Suggesting, Suggest a few changes, Suggestion cards, and Still there after a reopen.

storyboards.title: Rearrange a deck
storyboards.summary: Maria is turning last quarter's 8-slide update into this quarter's. She needs to move the results slide to the front, duplicate the chart slide to make a "before and after" pair, delete two out-of-date slides, and add a text box, a logo, and a callout shape. She works from the keyboard and the menus she knows from Google Slides and PowerPoint, and she expects Undo to rescue her.

scenes.heading: Open the deck
scenes.text: Maria opens "Q3 update" (8 slides). The filmstrip shows numbered thumbnails.

scenes.heading: Move a slide to the front
scenes.text: She clicks slide 6 ("Results") and presses Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Up. It becomes slide 1, and the filmstrip scrolls to keep it in view.

scenes.heading: Drag a group
scenes.text: She clicks slide 3, Shift-clicks slide 4, and drags both below slide 7. A line shows where they'll land, and both move together in their original order.

scenes.heading: Duplicate
scenes.text: With the chart slide selected she presses Cmd/Ctrl+D. A copy appears right after it and is selected. Slide › Duplicate slide and the thumbnail's right-click menu do the same.

scenes.heading: Delete two slides
scenes.text: She selects slides 7 and 8 and presses Delete. Both go, and a "2 slides deleted , Undo" notice appears.

scenes.heading: Undo and redo
scenes.text: Cmd/Ctrl+Z brings both back in place. Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Cmd/Ctrl+Y) deletes them again. Edit › Undo and Edit › Redo do the same.

scenes.heading: Insert from the menu
scenes.text: Insert › Text box places a text box in the middle of the slide, ready to type. Insert › Image opens a file picker, and the logo appears. Insert › Shape › Rounded rectangle adds a callout.

scenes.heading: Format from the menu
scenes.text: With the text box selected, Format › Text › Bold (Cmd/Ctrl+B) and Format › Align & indent › Center work on the text box.

scenes.heading: Copy and paste
scenes.text: She copies the callout with Cmd/Ctrl+C, clicks slide 2, and pastes with Cmd/Ctrl+V. It lands at the same position as the original, not the top-left corner. Edit › Cut, Copy, and Paste behave the same.

scenes.heading: Present
scenes.text: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter shows the deck in its new order.

storyboards.narration: Rearrange a deck. Maria is turning last quarter's 8-slide update into this quarter's. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the deck, Move a slide to the front, Drag a group, Duplicate, and Delete two slides.

storyboards.title: Give a deck a theme and transitions
storyboards.summary: Dev is making a 10-slide pitch for the community centre's fundraiser. The slides were written quickly in plain black and white, and some text boxes got their own fonts along the way. Dev wants one look across the whole deck: the centre's green, one heading font, and one body font. New slides should come out matching, and changing the theme later should restyle everything. A gentle fade between slides would be nice, as long as it doesn't take an afternoon.

scenes.heading: Open the deck
scenes.text: Dev opens "Fundraiser pitch". The slides are white with Arial text, and two text boxes use Georgia.

scenes.heading: Open themes
scenes.text: Dev clicks Theme in the toolbar (also Slide › Change theme). A side panel shows theme cards, each a small title slide drawn with the theme's background, accent colour, heading font, and body font.

scenes.heading: Preview and apply
scenes.text: Hovering "Meadow" (deep green, white headings in Montserrat, body text in Source Sans) previews it on the current slide. Moving away restores the slide. Clicking applies Meadow to every slide. Titles, body text, shapes, and the section slide all change, and the two Georgia text boxes switch to Source Sans too.

scenes.heading: Customize the theme
scenes.text: Under "Customize", Dev changes the accent colour to the centre's green (#2E7D32) with a colour picker. Every shape and accent on every slide follows.

scenes.heading: Keep a deliberate exception
scenes.text: On one slide Dev sets a quote in italic Georgia. A small "Overrides theme" marker appears in the Format panel with Reset to theme. Applying another theme later leaves this quote alone and restyles everything else.

scenes.heading: New slides match
scenes.text: Cmd/Ctrl+M adds a "Title & body" slide that already uses Meadow's colours and fonts. So do the layouts under Slide › Apply layout.

scenes.heading: Add transitions
scenes.text: Dev opens Slide › Transition. A panel offers None, Fade, Slide from right, and Push, with All slides already chosen and the duration at 0.4 s. Clicking Fade applies it to every slide (Apply to all slides does the same thing when a range is selected). Each thumbnail gets a small transition icon.

scenes.heading: Preview
scenes.text: Play in the panel previews the fade on the current slide. The slideshow (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) fades between every slide.

scenes.heading: Remove them all
scenes.text: Dev decides it's too much for one section, selects slides 4 to 6, and sets None. Those slides cut, and the others still fade.

scenes.heading: Hand off
scenes.text: Dev downloads the SuiteLeaf file. Opening it in a browser that already has the deck offers Keep both; the copy still has Meadow, the italic Georgia quote, and the same fades.

storyboards.narration: Give a deck a theme and transitions. Dev is making a 10-slide pitch for the community centre's fundraiser. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the deck, Open themes, Preview and apply, Customize the theme, and Keep a deliberate exception.

storyboards.title: Start from a template
storyboards.summary: Tomás runs a two-person bakery. This week he needs an invoice for a café that orders bread, notes for a meeting with his landlord, and a short deck for a farmers' market application. He doesn't want to design any of them from a blank page. Once his invoice looks right, he wants to reuse it every month without accidentally overwriting last month's.

scenes.heading: Home
scenes.text: Tomás opens SuiteLeaf. Under the three "New" cards there's a row titled "Start from a template" with Invoice, Meeting notes, Budget, Project tracker, Pitch deck, Letter, and Announcement (a second presentation, so slides aren't a single card), plus Template gallery ›.

scenes.heading: Browse
scenes.text: He clicks Template gallery. A full-page view groups templates by Documents, Spreadsheets, and Presentations, with a search box. He types "inv" and Invoice is the only result.

scenes.heading: Preview
scenes.text: Clicking Invoice opens a large preview of the sheet with its formulas visible as results ("Total $0.00"). Use template and Cancel sit underneath. Esc closes the preview without creating anything.

scenes.heading: Create
scenes.text: From Home he clicks Invoice, then Use template. A spreadsheet opens titled "Invoice" with the title box selected. He types "Invoice , Café Lune , October" and fills in sourdough (24 × $6.50) and rye (12 × $7). The total becomes $240.00.

scenes.heading: Make it his
scenes.text: He types "Hearth & Rye" in From and inserts a logo, then chooses File › Save as template. The dialog starts from the file's name with the month removed ("Invoice , Café Lune"). He names it "Bakery invoice" and clicks Save. It appears on the home row.

scenes.heading: Reuse next month
scenes.text: He clicks "Bakery invoice" on Home. A new file opens with the logo, the name, and the two lines. He retitles it "Invoice , Café Lune , November" and changes the sourdough quantity to 40; the total becomes $344.00. October is still 24 loaves and $240.00, and the template preview is too.

scenes.heading: From inside an editor
scenes.text: He starts Meeting notes, titles it "Landlord meeting", and adds "Rent is due Friday." under Next steps. File › New › From template opens the gallery filtered to Documents. He starts a fresh Meeting notes file.

scenes.heading: Offline
scenes.text: With the network off, he opens the gallery and creates a deck from "Pitch deck". The title slide opens.

scenes.heading: Tidy up
scenes.text: In the gallery, the ⋯ menu on "Bakery invoice" offers Rename and Remove. He removes it. October's invoice, November's invoice, the notes, and the pitch deck are still in the library.

storyboards.narration: Start from a template. Tomás runs a two-person bakery. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Home, Browse, Preview, Create, and Make it his.

storyboards.title: Count words and check spelling
storyboards.summary: Amara is finishing a 1,500-word history essay. The limit excludes the reference list, and she needs to know how long her introduction is on its own. She types fast, and her essay is full of names ("Danquah", "Ghana's") and words the dictionary doesn't know ("kente"). She wants to fix real typos quickly without wading through false alarms, and without the checker forgetting her choices.

scenes.heading: Open the essay
scenes.text: Amara opens "Independence essay". The status bar already shows "1,612 words".

scenes.heading: Count a selection
scenes.text: She selects the introduction. The status bar changes to "318 of 1,612 words" while the selection lasts.

scenes.heading: Word count details
scenes.text: She opens Tools › Word count (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C). A dialog lists words, characters, characters without spaces, paragraphs, and pages, for the selection and for the whole document.

scenes.heading: Exclude the references
scenes.text: In the dialog she chooses "Stop counting at heading: References". The document total drops to 1,488. She leaves "Count footnotes" unticked. The status bar reads "1,488 words (excludes References)". She closes the essay and opens it again; the exclusion is still there.

scenes.heading: Spelling as she types
scenes.text: She retypes "movement" as "movment". It is underlined on this computer. Right-clicking shows "movement" first, then "Add to dictionary" and "Ignore". Clicking "movement" fixes it.

scenes.heading: Teach it a word
scenes.text: Names such as "Danquah" are never underlined. "kente", the cloth, is. She right-clicks it and chooses Add to dictionary. The other "kente" in the essay loses its underline too.

scenes.heading: Check the whole essay
scenes.text: Tools › Spelling opens a panel that steps through issues one by one. After the first Enter it shows "2 of 5 , recieve to receive", with Change, Ignore, and Add to dictionary. Enter keeps going, and the bold on "separate" stays.

scenes.heading: Change her mind
scenes.text: On the last issue she adds "teh" by mistake. Tools › Personal dictionary lists "kente" and "teh". She removes "teh", it is underlined again, and she corrects it to "the".

scenes.heading: Offline
scenes.text: The status bar still reads "1,488 words (excludes References)", nothing unknown is left, and none of the text left the computer.

storyboards.narration: Count words and check spelling. Amara is finishing a 1,500-word history essay. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the essay, Count a selection, Word count details, Exclude the references, and Spelling as she types.

storyboards.title: Add a table of contents and footnotes
storyboards.summary: Kwame is writing a 20-page grant report for a youth football charity. The funder wants a table of contents on page 2, sources cited in footnotes, and the report as a Word file. Kwame keeps moving sections around until the last minute, so the contents page has to keep up without him remembering to refresh it, and the footnotes have to arrive in Word as real footnotes.

scenes.heading: Open the report
scenes.text: Kwame opens "Grant report 2026" from his files. It has a title page, a page break, and 8 Heading 1 and Heading 2 sections. The outline lists them on the left.

scenes.heading: Insert the contents
scenes.text: On page 2 he chooses Insert › Table of contents › With page numbers (two clicks). A table appears listing every heading, indented by level, with dotted leaders and page numbers.

scenes.heading: It follows the document
scenes.text: He renames "Results" to "What we achieved", adds a Heading 2 "Coaching hours", and cuts the "Budget" section and pastes it above "What we achieved". Within a second the table shows the new names, the new entry, and the new order and page numbers. There's no Refresh button.

scenes.heading: Use it as links
scenes.text: Clicking "Budget" in the table scrolls to that heading. Options on the table switches between page numbers and plain links, and between Heading 1 only and levels 1 to 3.

scenes.heading: Add a footnote
scenes.text: After "attendance rose 40%" he presses Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+F. A superscript appears at the cursor, and he types the source in the note.

scenes.heading: More footnotes
scenes.text: He adds two more later in the report, then inserts one earlier. The numbers update to 1 to 4 in reading order. Clicking a number in the text jumps to its note, and clicking the note's number jumps back.

scenes.heading: Print layout
scenes.text: The notes that belong on a page sit together at the bottom, under a short rule. A note taller than that band continues on the next page.

scenes.heading: Export for the funder
scenes.text: File › Export DOCX. The file Word opens has a real table-of-contents field (References › Update Table) and real footnotes (footnotes.xml, w:footnoteReference).

scenes.heading: Back from Word
scenes.text: The funder's officer adds an endnote and returns the file. Kwame opens it: the contents, the four footnotes, and the endnote are linked to their markers. The import summary reads "4 footnotes, 1 endnote, 1 table of contents". Endnotes stay endnotes.

storyboards.narration: Add a table of contents and footnotes. Kwame is writing a 20-page grant report for a youth football charity. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the report, Insert the contents, It follows the document, Use it as links, and Add a footnote.

storyboards.title: Find any command
storyboards.summary: Priya has used Google Workspace for years and has just switched to SuiteLeaf. She knows what she wants to do ("strikethrough", "freeze the top row", "duplicate this slide") but not where SuiteLeaf keeps it, and she'd rather type than hunt through menus. She also wants to learn the shortcuts for the things she does every day.

scenes.heading: Docs: search the menus
scenes.text: In "Quarterly Report", Priya selects a phrase and presses Option+/ (Alt+/ on Windows). A search box opens over the menu bar. She types "strike". "Format › Strikethrough , ⌘⇧X" is the top result. She presses Enter, and the phrase is struck through.

scenes.heading: Plain words work
scenes.text: She types "count". "Tools › Word count" comes up even though she didn't type "word". "page numbers" finds the page setup options.

scenes.heading: Unavailable commands explain themselves
scenes.text: With nothing selected she types "link". "Insert › Link" appears greyed with "Select text to add a link".

scenes.heading: Shortcut list
scenes.text: She presses ⌘/ (Ctrl+/ on Windows). A "Keyboard shortcuts" dialog lists Docs shortcuts grouped as Text formatting, Paragraphs, Editing, Navigation, and Files, with a search box. Keys are shown as ⌘, ⌥, and ⇧ on her Mac.

scenes.heading: Sheets
scenes.text: In the "Sample budget" she clicks the toolbar's Menus pill, types "freeze", and picks "View › Freeze › 1 row". The header row freezes. ⌘/ shows the Sheets shortcut list, including the formula shortcuts.

scenes.heading: Slides
scenes.text: In a deck, Option+/ then "dup" runs "Slide › Duplicate slide". Help › Keyboard shortcuts shows the filmstrip and slideshow keys (←/ to , B, W, S, Esc).

scenes.heading: Recent commands
scenes.text: Opening the search again with nothing typed lists her last few commands first.

scenes.heading: Every listed shortcut works
scenes.text: She tries ⌘D in Slides and ⌘⇧X in Docs, as listed. Both do what the dialog says.

storyboards.narration: Find any command. Priya has used Google Workspace for years and has just switched to SuiteLeaf. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Docs: search the menus, Plain words work, Unavailable commands explain themselves, Shortcut list, and Sheets.

storyboards.title: Dropdown lists in a sheet
storyboards.summary: Lena keeps the food bank's volunteer roster. The Status column is a mess of "confirmed", "Confirmed ", "yes", and "tbc", so she can't filter it. She wants a dropdown with three choices, each in its own colour, that stops people typing anything else. When the committee adds a "Waitlist" status in a month, she wants to add it and rename "Tentative" to "Maybe" without repainting every cell.

scenes.heading: Open the roster
scenes.text: Lena opens "Volunteer roster". Column C, Status, has 40 rows of inconsistent text: Confirmed, "Confirmed ", confirmed, Tentative, yes, tbc.

scenes.heading: Make a dropdown
scenes.text: She selects C2:C41 and chooses Insert › Dropdown. A side panel opens with the options already filled in from the distinct values, trimmed and grouped case-insensitively: Confirmed, Tentative, yes, tbc. Reject other values is already on.

scenes.heading: Tidy the options
scenes.text: She deletes yes and tbc, adds "Can't make it", and picks green, amber, and grey. A preview chip next to each option shows the colour with readable text. She clicks Done.

scenes.heading: Fix the leftovers
scenes.text: Cells that don't match get a red corner, and a notice says "6 cells don't match the list" with Review. Review steps through them , yes and tbc , offering Confirmed, with Accept and Skip. Accepting writes Confirmed and its green chip.

scenes.heading: Pick from the cell
scenes.text: In C5 she types "ma". The list filters to "Can't make it", and Enter picks it.

scenes.heading: Typing something else
scenes.text: In C6 she types "maybe" and presses Enter. The cell is refused, with "Choose Confirmed, Tentative, or Can't make it." Helen stays Confirmed.

scenes.heading: Rename an option
scenes.text: She reopens Data › Data validation, renames Tentative to Maybe, and adds Waitlist in blue. Every cell that said Tentative now says Maybe and keeps its amber chip. She sets Priya to Waitlist.

scenes.heading: Filter by status
scenes.text: Data › Create a filter, then the Status filter lists exactly Confirmed, Maybe, Can't make it, and Waitlist.

scenes.heading: Send to Excel
scenes.text: File › Export XLSX. The column has a list validation with those four options and error style stop. Opening the workbook again restores the dropdown and the reject setting. Chip colours stay in the SuiteLeaf file; Excel has no place for them.

storyboards.narration: Dropdown lists in a sheet. Lena keeps the food bank's volunteer roster. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Open the roster, Make a dropdown, Tidy the options, Fix the leftovers, and Pick from the cell.

storyboards.title: Clean up messy data
storyboards.summary: Omar is treasurer of a small charity. He has pasted three months of donations from the payment site's email receipts into one sheet. Names have stray spaces, the "Donor" column reads "Okafor, Ade" where he needs separate first and last names, and people who gave twice appear twice. He needs a clean list of unique donors for thank-you letters. He's nervous about deleting the wrong rows, so he wants to see what will go before it goes, and to be able to undo it.

scenes.heading: Open the donations
scenes.text: Omar opens "Donations Q3": columns Date, Donor, Email, Amount, Gift Aid. There are 112 rows. He jumps to the last receipt and back.

scenes.heading: Trim
scenes.text: He selects B1:C113 and chooses Data › Data cleanup › Trim whitespace. A notice reads "Trimmed 23 cells (including 4 non-breaking spaces)".

scenes.heading: Split names
scenes.text: He selects B2:B113 and chooses Data › Split text to columns. A panel detects "Comma" as the separator and previews two columns, "Okafor" and "Ade". It warns "Column C isn't empty: insert 1 column?" He keeps Insert columns, renames the headers Last name and First name, and clicks Split.

scenes.heading: Find duplicates
scenes.text: He selects the whole table and chooses Data › Data cleanup › Remove duplicates. The dialog detects the header row and lists the columns. He clicks Only on Email.

scenes.heading: Choose which to keep
scenes.text: Under "Keep" he picks "The row with the most filled cells", because some later receipts include the Gift Aid flag. Ignore case stays on.

scenes.heading: Preview
scenes.text: The dialog says "9 duplicate rows will be removed, 103 will remain", and those 9 rows are highlighted in the sheet behind it. The complete Gift Aid copy of the same person is not highlighted. He scrolls to check two more.

scenes.heading: Remove
scenes.text: He clicks Remove. A notice that stays until he closes it reads "Removed 9 duplicate rows , 103 remain , Undo".

scenes.heading: Undo and redo

storyboards.title: Insert a function with help
storyboards.summary: Ben teaches PE and keeps fitness-test results for his class in a sheet: name, 12-minute run in metres, sit-ups, and whether each student passed. He knows he wants "the average", "how many passed", and "a pass if they ran over 2,000 m", but not the function names or the order their arguments go in. He wants SuiteLeaf to help him write each formula without leaving the sheet, and to answer quick questions without writing a formula at all.

scenes.heading: Open the results
scenes.text: Ben opens "Year 9 fitness". B2:B29 is metres, C2:C29 is sit-ups, and D is an empty "Pass?" column.

scenes.heading: Quick answers
scenes.text: He selects B2:B29. The status bar shows "Sum 58,940 , Average 2,105 , Min 1,520 , Max 2,710 , Count 28". Hovering Average offers Insert below, and one click puts =AVERAGE(B2:B29) in B30 (2,105).

scenes.heading: Browse functions
scenes.text: He clicks D2 and opens Insert › Function. The menu shows a short "Common" list (SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, COUNTIF, IF, MIN, MAX, ROUND, VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP), then categories (Math, Statistical, Logical, Text, Date, Lookup) and "Search functions…".

scenes.heading: Find by meaning
scenes.text: In Search he types "if a condition". IF is the top result, described as "Returns one value if a condition is true and another if it's false". He picks it.

scenes.heading: Write with help
scenes.text: D2 enters edit mode with =IF(. A help panel docks in the formula bar, beside the formula, and the grid starts below it. It shows IF(logicalexpression, valueiftrue, valueiffalse) with the current argument in bold, a one-line description of it, and an example. As he types B2>2000, the bold moves to valueif_true.

scenes.heading: Finish and fill
scenes.text: He completes =IF(B2>2000,"Pass","Not yet"), presses Enter, and drags the fill handle down the class. The panel closes when he leaves the cell. Rows that ran over 2,000 m say Pass.

scenes.heading: Count the passes
scenes.text: In D30 he types =COUNTIF(. The panel explains range and criterion, with the example COUNTIF(A1:A10, ">20"). He finishes =COUNTIF(D2:D29,"Pass") and gets 19.

scenes.heading: Use the toolbar
scenes.text: He selects C2:C29 and clicks Σ in the toolbar. =SUM(C2:C29) goes into C30 (698), below the selection, and the sit-up counts stay put.

scenes.heading: Make room
scenes.text: On a later formula he collapses the help panel with its chevron. The next formula stays collapsed. Shift+F1 toggles it, and F1 opens the same panel instead of another page.

scenes.heading: The minutes

scenes.heading: Click the header
scenes.text: He double-clicks that header. The minutes dim, the whole header is selected, and a label says "Header , all pages". Page setup does not open.

scenes.heading: Type
scenes.text: He types "October minutes". The page shows it before he leaves the header.

scenes.heading: Back to the minutes

scenes.heading: Every page
scenes.text: Page 1 says "October minutes" too. This document has one shared header.

scenes.heading: The footer

scenes.heading: Escape
scenes.text: Escape closes the footer. "Draft" and the number both stay.

scenes.heading: Save
scenes.text: He reopens the file. The header still says "October minutes", and the footer still says "Draft" next to the number.

storyboards.narration: Edit the header on the page. Ben has the minutes open and wants to change the running header from "Garden club minutes" to "October minutes". Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The minutes, Click the header, Type, Back to the minutes, and Every page.

storyboards.title: Choose a page number
storyboards.summary: Ben's minutes always print "1 / 3" in the bottom right. The committee wants "Page 2" at the bottom center, and the first page should start at 1 even when there is a cover. Page setup only offers a checkbox, and the hint says the number is always "1 / 3" at the bottom right.

scenes.heading: The default
scenes.text: Ben opens "Minutes". Page 1 ends with "1 / 2" at the bottom right, and page 2 ends with "2 / 2" there too.

scenes.heading: The choice
scenes.text: Page setup, one dialog, shows the format and the position next to the page-numbers checkbox. He picks "Page 1" and Bottom center. The hint and the little page preview follow.

scenes.heading: The page

scenes.heading: The footer

scenes.heading: Top right

scenes.heading: Save
scenes.text: He reopens the file. The position and the "Page N" wording are unchanged.

scenes.heading: Off, then on

storyboards.narration: Choose a page number. Ben's minutes always print "1 / 3" in the bottom right. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The default, The choice, The page, The footer, and Top right.

storyboards.title: Describe a photo
storyboards.summary: Lena's sign-up note has a photo of the seed-swap stall. A member who uses a screen reader hears nothing useful about that picture. Google Docs lets her write alt text that stays with the image. SuiteLeaf exports an alt field, but there is no way to type it.

scenes.heading: The photo
scenes.text: Lena starts the sign-up note and adds the stall photo. The file on her camera is named IMG_2044. The photo has no description.

scenes.heading: Write it
scenes.text: She selects the photo. Alt text sits beside it, clear of the corner handles, and the field starts empty. She types "Neighbors trading seed packets at the spring stall." and clicks Apply.

scenes.heading: See it
scenes.text: She clicks away and selects the photo again. The same sentence is there, not the file name.

scenes.heading: A blank description
scenes.text: She clears the text and applies. The photo stays. The description is empty, not a leftover filename.

scenes.heading: Keep it
scenes.text: She writes the sentence back. That is the description she wants to keep.

scenes.heading: Save and Word
scenes.text: She leaves and opens the note again. The sentence is still on the photo. File › Export DOCX writes that sentence as the image's alt text.

storyboards.narration: Describe a photo. Lena's sign-up note has a photo of the seed-swap stall. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The photo, Write it, See it, A blank description, and Keep it.

storyboards.title: Leave room for the binding
storyboards.summary: Ben is printing the minutes double-sided and stapling them on the left. The text runs into the staple. Page setup has one margin for every edge. There is no extra gutter on the inside edge, so odd pages need more room on the left and even pages need more room on the right.

scenes.heading: Equal margins
scenes.text: Ben opens "Minutes". Every page has the same gap on the left and the right. The first line starts at the same distance from the left edge on page 2 and page 3.

scenes.heading: A gutter
scenes.text: In Page setup he sets Gutter to 0.5 in. Page 3, an odd page, starts further from the left. Page 2, an even page, starts further from the right. The outside edge stays at the original margin.

scenes.heading: The letterhead
scenes.text: Page 1, if Different first page is on, still uses the gutter on the left, because a cover is bound on the left too.

scenes.heading: Zero
scenes.text: He sets the gutter back to 0. Pages 2 and 3 line up again.

scenes.heading: Save
scenes.text: He reopens the file. The 0.5 in gutter is back, and the inside edges are still wider.

storyboards.narration: Leave room for the binding. Ben is printing the minutes double-sided and stapling them on the left. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Equal margins, A gutter, The letterhead, Zero, and Save.

storyboards.title: Open a cropped Word picture

scenes.heading: The Word file

scenes.heading: Round trip
scenes.text: She crops the parking lot out again and chooses File to Export DOCX. She opens that file. The stall is still the frame, and the full photo is still in the package.

storyboards.title: Set each margin

scenes.heading: One margin

scenes.heading: Four fields

scenes.heading: Save

storyboards.narration: Set each margin. Ben is matching the town council's template. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through One margin, Four fields, The page, A bad value, and Save.

storyboards.title: Change every copy in a sheet
storyboards.summary: Sam's decisions sheet says "recieve" in four cells. Right-click fixes one cell (storyboard 63). Tools › Spelling then walks the other three one at a time. He wants one action that fixes every copy, and a way to leave a cell that used the word on purpose.

scenes.heading: Four cells
scenes.text: Sam opens "Decisions". B2, B4, B7, and B9 contain "recieve". B6 contains "seperate", which he wants to keep.

scenes.heading: The menu
scenes.text: He right-clicks "recieve" in B2. Besides "receive", the menu has "Change all to receive".

scenes.heading: A preview
scenes.text: Choosing Change all highlights and lists the four cells. B6 is not in the list. He cancels, and the cells stay "recieve".

scenes.heading: Apply
scenes.text: Tools › Spelling has the same Change all. He confirms. All four cells say "receive", and the check moves on to "seperate". One Undo restores all four. Redo fixes them again.

scenes.heading: Leave one
scenes.text: He undoes that, then chooses Ignore this cell on B9. The other copies stay underlined. Change all from B2 lists the other three, fixes them, and leaves B9.

scenes.heading: Save
scenes.text: He reopens the file. The three corrections remain, and B9 is still "recieve" and not underlined.

storyboards.narration: Change every copy in a sheet. Sam's decisions sheet says "recieve" in four cells. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Four cells, The menu, A preview, Apply, and Leave one.

storyboards.narration: Space the lines. Priya is writing the garden-club minutes. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The minutes, The choice, The page, Double, and Save and Word.

scenes.heading: The text stays put

scenes.text: Dragging a corner changes the size and keeps the proportions. The logo does not snap back to the pixel size.

scenes.text: She exports .docx and opens it again. Both pictures keep the size she had on the page.

storyboards.narration: Open a picture at its page size. The printer sent Lena a Word letter. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The letter, The text stays put, She can still resize, A full-width photo, and Round trip.

storyboards.title: Put a picture beside the text

scenes.heading: The letter
scenes.text: Lena opens a document where the logo is a block. "Dear friend," starts on the next line.

scenes.text: She selects the logo and chooses Wrap text › Left. The greeting moves up and runs to the right of the logo.

scenes.text: Wrap text › Break text puts the logo on its own line again, and the greeting returns underneath.

scenes.text: She opens a .docx whose picture is already wrapped square on the left. It opens beside the paragraph, not as a full-width block, and the import note no longer says floating placement may differ for that picture.

scenes.text: She downloads the SuiteLeaf file and opens the copy. The logo is still beside the greeting.

storyboards.title: Group columns
storyboards.summary: Rosa's budget has the category name in column A and twelve month columns after it. She can already collapse month rows (storyboard 58). scenes.heading: The year across
scenes.text: Rosa opens "Rent budget". Column A is the category. Columns B to M are the months. Column N is the year total, past the right edge.

scenes.heading: Group the months
scenes.text: She selects columns B to M, not A and not N, and chooses Data › Group columns. A minus control appears above those columns. Category and the year total stay.

scenes.heading: Collapse
scenes.text: She clicks the minus. Columns B to M hide. Column N slides into view beside column A. The year total is unchanged.

scenes.heading: One month
scenes.text: She expands the group and hides every month except January. February is hidden. January and the year total stay.

scenes.heading: Undo
scenes.text: One Undo removes the column group. All twelve months are visible again.

scenes.heading: The label
scenes.text: She selects only column A and chooses Group columns. The dialog says there is nothing to group, and column A stays visible.

scenes.heading: Save
scenes.text: Redo puts the group back, still open on January. She leaves and opens Rent budget again. January is still the only month, and the year total is still beside the category.

scenes.heading: Rows still group
scenes.text: She groups the Rent and Food rows and collapses them. Those rows hide. January and the year total stay, and the other months stay hidden.

storyboards.narration: Group columns. Rosa's budget has the category name in column A and twelve month columns after it. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The year across, Group the months, Collapse, One month, and Undo.

scenes.heading: The minutes
scenes.text: Priya opens "Garden club minutes". Two pages, and no word behind the text.

scenes.heading: The word

scenes.text: Page 1 and page 2 both show DRAFT behind the paragraphs, large and faint. She adds "The vote was unanimous." The word stays where it was, and it is not in the paragraph.

scenes.text: She changes the field to FINAL. Both pages update. DRAFT is gone.

scenes.heading: Clear

scenes.heading: Save and Word

storyboards.narration: Mark a draft. Priya's garden-club minutes are not ready to send. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The minutes, The word, Every page, A different word, and Clear.

scenes.heading: Save
scenes.text: She downloads the SuiteLeaf file and opens the copy. The photo is still between the words.

scenes.heading: The newsletter
scenes.text: Nia opens "Garden club news". The heading "Garden club news for the March plant sale" sits above three short items, all in one column.

scenes.heading: Back to one

storyboards.narration: Two columns for the news. Nia writes the garden-club newsletter. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The newsletter, The body only, The page, Back to one, and Save and Word.

storyboards.narration: Start numbering at. Ben's minutes are pages 4 and 5 of a packet that already has a cover and two letters. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The minutes, Start at 4, The footer stays, A cover, and Off and on.

storyboards.summary: Maya put the vote on the Minutes tab and the agenda on the first tab. She later searches for "compost" while she is looking at the agenda. Find today only reads the tab she is on, and so does SuiteDrive search. The decision is in the file and she is told it is not there. Google Docs search can reach other tabs, but the hit does not say which tab it is in, so she still has to hunt.

scenes.heading: Two tabs
scenes.text: Maya opens "October meeting". Agenda says "Call to order. Treasurer's report." Minutes says "Voted to buy compost." She is looking at Agenda.

scenes.heading: Find
scenes.text: She opens Find and replace and types "compost".

scenes.text: The Minutes tab becomes selected. "Voted to buy compost." is on the page, and the find bar says the match is on Minutes.

storyboards.narration: Find the decision on the other tab. Maya put the vote on the Minutes tab and the agenda on the first tab. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Two tabs, Find, The other tab, and The agenda is still there.

storyboards.title: Take the whole meeting with you

scenes.heading: Both tabs
scenes.text: Maya opens "October meeting". Agenda says "Call to order. Treasurer's report." Minutes says "Voted to buy compost." She leaves Agenda selected.

scenes.heading: Export
scenes.text: She chooses File › Export TXT. She does not switch to Minutes first.

scenes.heading: The whole meeting
scenes.text: The downloaded text contains Agenda, the call to order, Minutes, and the compost vote, in that order.

scenes.heading: The document is unchanged
scenes.text: Agenda is still the selected tab. The vote is still only on Minutes.

storyboards.narration: Take the whole meeting with you. Maya finished the October meeting. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through Both tabs, Export, The whole meeting, and The document is unchanged.

storyboards.title: See the vote that changed
storyboards.summary: Maya changed the October minutes from compost to mulch and left the agenda alone. She opens version history while she is looking at the agenda. Today the compare only reads the first tab, so it can say nothing changed. She needs to see that the vote changed, and which tab it was on, before she decides whether to put the old wording back.

scenes.heading: Two tabs, one saved version
scenes.text: Maya creates "October meeting". Agenda says "Call to order. Treasurer's report." Minutes says "Voted to buy compost." She saves a version she can return to.

scenes.heading: Only the vote changes
scenes.text: On Minutes she replaces compost with mulch. Agenda is not edited. She saves again.

scenes.heading: History
scenes.text: She opens version history and selects the earlier version. The summary says a paragraph changed, and it names Minutes. Agenda is not listed as changed.

scenes.heading: The wording
scenes.text: She looks at Minutes in the compare. The old vote is struck and the new vote is marked as added. She looks at Agenda and the call to order has no strike or add.

scenes.heading: She does not restore
scenes.text: She closes history. The live minutes still say mulch.

She wants a document she can check, and she does not want anything emailed.

scenes.heading: The list

scenes.heading: The letter

scenes.heading: One letter each

storyboards.title: Use the roster on the server

scenes.text: She points the letter at {{Bed}} and merges again. The dialog says Bed is not a column, and no extra document is created.

storyboards.title: Put the fee chart in the minutes
storyboards.summary: Maya wants the plot-fee numbers in the October minutes. In Google Docs she must first build a chart in the spreadsheet, then insert that chart, and the link is easy to miss. An Update button floats over the chart and is easy to skip, so the minutes keep last month's numbers. If someone deletes the spreadsheet, the chart becomes a broken picture with no explanation.

scenes.heading: The fees
scenes.text: Maya has a spreadsheet "Plot fees". The first row is Fee and Amount. Dues is 40. Compost is 15.

scenes.heading: Insert
scenes.text: In "October meeting" she chooses Insert chart and picks Plot fees. She does not build a chart in the spreadsheet first.

scenes.heading: The bars
scenes.text: The minutes show a bar for Dues at 40 and a bar for Compost at 15. Under the chart, a line says From Plot fees.

scenes.heading: The number changes
scenes.text: She sets Compost to 25 in the spreadsheet and returns to the minutes. The chart still says 15 until she clicks Update. It then says 25. Dues stays 40.

scenes.heading: The sheet goes away
scenes.text: She removes Plot fees from the library and clicks Update again. The bars stay at the last numbers, and the line says the spreadsheet is missing. The minutes are not blank.

storyboards.narration: Put the fee chart in the minutes. Maya wants the plot-fee numbers in the October minutes. Watch as SuiteLeaf walks through The fees, Insert, The bars, The number changes, and The sheet goes away.

storyboards.title: Send the minutes with the fees still in them
storyboards.summary: Maya put the plot-fee chart in the October minutes. She exports a Word file for the club email. Today that file drops the chart, so the email has the prose and not the numbers. In Google Docs the chart becomes a picture. The numbers are not text, the source file is not named, and a screen reader skips the fees.

scenes.heading: The chart is in the minutes
scenes.text: October meeting shows Dues at 40, Compost at 15, and From Plot fees.

scenes.heading: Export
scenes.text: She chooses File › Export DOCX. She does not copy the numbers by hand.

scenes.heading: The Word file has the fees
scenes.text: The download contains the words Dues, 40, Compost, 15, and Plot fees, as text she can select, not only as a picture.

scenes.heading: The minutes stay
scenes.text: The chart is still on the page in SuiteLeaf, with the same numbers.
